info.name: FixHomi Auth Service (jauth)
info.description:
# FixHomi Auth Service (jauth) — local collection

Every endpoint of the Java auth service, ordered as a walkthrough. Built against the code on `main`
and verified end-to-end against a local instance.

## Setup
1. Start the service: `cp .env.local.example .env`, set `JWT_SECRET`, `./run.sh local`
   (full guide: `docs/onboarding/01-local-setup.md`).
2. Import this collection and `FixHomi_Auth_Local.postman_environment.json`; select **FixHomi Auth – Local**.
3. Run the folders **in order**. Test scripts save tokens/ids into the environment.

## OTPs and emailed tokens
In the `local` profile nothing is sent. The service console prints:
- `OTP CODE: 123456` → paste into the `OTP` variable before a *verify* request
- `TOKEN: ...` under `EMAIL TYPE: Email Verification` → `EMAIL_VERIFY_TOKEN`
- `TOKEN: ...` under `EMAIL TYPE: Password Reset` → `RESET_TOKEN`

## Auth
Collection-level auth is `Bearer {{ACCESS_TOKEN}}` (the USER from folder 01). Public endpoints are set to *No Auth*
on purpose: the JWT filter also runs on public paths and rejects a token that belongs to a deleted account.
Admin requests use `{{ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN}}`, SUPPORT requests `{{SUPPORT_ACCESS_TOKEN}}`.

## Rate limits
Per IP: 10/min on login-type paths, 5/min on OTP-sending paths, 100/min otherwise.
For the Collection Runner set `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false` in `.env` and restart.

item.name: 00 · Health
item.description: Public liveness endpoints. Start here to confirm the service is up.

request.description: Public. `AuthController.health()` → `{status, message}`. Not rate-limited (GET).
Public (`/actuator/health/**` is in the permit list). Used by Render's health check and the mobile app's `authInfraService`.
Public. App name/version from `info.*` in `application.yaml`.

item.name: 01 · Register & password login
item.description:
Email/password registration and login. Every successful call returns a `LoginResponse` and the test script stores
`ACCESS_TOKEN`, `REFRESH_TOKEN` and `USER_ID` in the environment, so the following folders work without copy-paste.

Rate-limit bucket: **auth** (10 requests/min per IP).

request.description:
Public. `AuthController.register` → `AuthService.register`. Returns **201** + `LoginResponse`.

- `role` must be `USER` or `SERVICE_PROVIDER` (anything else → 403 *Invalid Role*).
- `password`: 8–100 chars with upper, lower, digit and one of `@$!%*?&#^()_+-=`.
- `phoneNumber` is optional; stored normalised to 10 digits (`+919876543210` → `9876543210`).

The pre-request script generates a fresh email + phone every run so you never hit 409 duplicates.
Same endpoint, `role: SERVICE_PROVIDER`. Tokens are saved as `PROVIDER_*` so they don't overwrite the USER's.

RBAC guard: public registration only allows `USER` / `SERVICE_PROVIDER`
(`AuthService.register`). ADMIN, IT_ADMIN and SUPPORT can only be created by an admin via `POST /api/admin/users`.
Expected: **403** `{"error":"Invalid Role", ...}`.

Public. `AuthService.login`. 5 wrong passwords lock the identifier for 15 minutes (429).
Note: the lookup is case-sensitive on the email you send — send it lowercase.

Public. `AuthService.loginWithPhone`. Phone pattern `^\+?[1-9]\d{6,14}$`.
Accounts created by phone signup have no password, so they cannot use this — they use OTP login.

Public. Exchanges the refresh token for a **new access token and a new refresh token**; the old refresh token is
revoked (`RefreshTokenService.rotateRefreshToken`). Refresh tokens live 60 days, access tokens 24 h.

The pre-request script keeps the old token in `PREV_REFRESH_TOKEN` for the next request.

item.name: Refresh again with the OLD token (45 s grace window)

request.description:
Replays the token that was just rotated. Within `jwt.refresh-token.rotation-grace-seconds` (45 s) the service returns
the **same successor** instead of 401 — this protects the mobile app when two requests refresh at the same time.
After 45 s the same call returns 401. Send this within 45 s of the previous request.

exec: pm.test('Returns the same successor refresh token', function () {

item.name: 02 · Who am I (token introspection)
item.description: Endpoints that describe the caller. All require `Authorization: Bearer {{ACCESS_TOKEN}}` (inherited from the collection).

request.description:
`TokenController` → `TokenValidationService`. Returns the claims decoded from the JWT
(`userId`, `email` = `sub`, `role`, `tokenType`, `issuedAt`, `expiresAt`). The role here is the **JWT** role.
See `docs/onboarding/08-walkthrough-send-otp-and-validate-token.md` for the full request lifecycle.
Same service call and response as `/api/token/validate`.

`SessionController.validateToken`. Unlike `/api/token/validate` this reads the **database** user row:
returns `role` from the DB plus `isEmailVerified` / `isPhoneVerified`.

`UserController.getCurrentUserProfile` → `UserProfileResponse` (includes `hasPassword`, timestamps).
The mobile app and the Node backend both call this.

item.name: 03 · Verify my phone & email (logged in)
item.description:
Marks the logged-in user's stored phone/email as verified. Phone OTPs and email links are printed to the console by
the stub providers in the `local` profile.

request.description:
JWT required. `PhoneVerificationService.sendOtp` — sends an OTP to the phone already on the account.
400 if the account has no phone or it is already verified. Bucket: **otp** (5/min).

JWT required. Sets `isPhoneVerified=true`. 3 attempts per OTP, 5-minute expiry.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.

JWT required. `EmailVerificationService`. The console prints `TOKEN: ...` and `VERIFICATION URL: ...`.
Copy the token into `EMAIL_VERIFY_TOKEN` (or simply open the URL in a browser). One request per 5 minutes (429).

Public. Returns an **HTML page** (status 200 even on failure) that redirects to the app deep link
`fixhomi://email-verified?...`. The token is stored hashed (SHA-256) in the DB, so it is only visible in the console.

item.name: 04 · Passwordless OTP login
item.description:
Login for an **existing** account with a one-time code (`OtpLoginController` → `OtpLoginService`).
Unknown phone/email → 404 `USER_NOT_FOUND` (sign-up is a separate flow, folder 05).
Errors here use the shape `{success:false, code, message}` rather than the global `ErrorResponse`.

request.description:
Public. Max 3 sends per phone per 5 minutes (429 `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`). Full walkthrough of this request:
`docs/onboarding/08-walkthrough-send-otp-and-validate-token.md`.

Public. Returns a full `LoginResponse`.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.
Public. Console prints `EMAIL TYPE: Login OTP` with `OTP CODE: ...`.

Public. Also marks the email verified.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.

item.name: 05 · Phone signup (USER only)
item.description:
Creates a **new USER** account from a phone number alone (`PhoneSignupController` → `PhoneSignupService`).
The role is hard-coded to USER; the account has no email and no password. No user row exists until verify succeeds.

request.description: Public. 409 `ALREADY_REGISTERED` if a verified active account already has this phone.

Public. Returns `LoginResponse` with `isNewUser: true`, `role: USER`, `email: null`.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.

item.name: 06 · My account (/api/users)
item.description: Self-service account operations. All act on the caller only (the user id comes from the JWT, never from the body).

request.description:
`UserService.updateProfile`. `fullName` 2–100 chars. A `phoneNumber` in this body is **ignored** unless the account has
no phone at all (legacy add-only path for old app builds) — use the phone-change endpoints instead.

`UserService.setEmail`. Stores the email unverified and sends a verification link (console).
409 if another active account uses it. The test script makes the new email the current `USER_EMAIL`.

item.name: Change phone · send OTP to new number

request.description: `PhoneVerificationService.sendChangeOtp`. The current number stays until the new one is verified.

Replaces the number and marks it verified in one step.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.

`UserService.changePassword`. When the account already had a password, **all its refresh tokens are revoked**
(existing access tokens keep working until they expire). Accounts without a password may omit `currentPassword`.
The next request logs in again with the new password.
Fresh tokens after the password change.

item.name: 07 · Forgot / reset password
item.description:
Three independent ways to reset a forgotten password (`PasswordResetService`). Each success revokes all refresh tokens,
and each test script stores the new password in `USER_PASSWORD`.

request.description:
Public. Always 200 (does not reveal whether the email exists). Console prints
`EMAIL TYPE: Password Reset (Mobile + Web)` and `TOKEN: ...` — copy it into `RESET_TOKEN`.
Public. 200 if the token exists, is unused and less than 1 hour old; otherwise 400.
Public. Marks the token used, sets the password, revokes refresh tokens.
Public. 404 `USER_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown phone or an account without a password.

Public.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.
Public. Console prints the code under `EMAIL TYPE: Login OTP` (same template as login).

Public.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.
Fresh tokens.

item.name: 08 · Sessions & trusted devices
item.description:
`SessionController`. Trusted devices are stored per user in `trusted_devices`.
Note: no login flow currently writes `user_sessions` rows, so the session list is empty and revoking a session by id
returns 401 "Session not found" — see `docs/onboarding/10-behaviours-and-gotchas.md`.

request.description: Optional `X-Device-Id` header marks `isCurrentSession`.
Upsert by (user, deviceId).
Body optional. With `exceptDeviceId`, keeps that device's session.
Returns 401 "Session not found" today because no sessions are recorded at login.

item.name: 09 · Admin (ADMIN / IT_ADMIN)
item.description:
`AdminUserController` — `/api/admin/**` requires role ADMIN or IT_ADMIN (URL rule in `SecurityConfig` **and**
`@PreAuthorize` on every method). Requests in this folder use `{{ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN}}`.

Locally, the `local` profile seeds `admin@fixhomi.local` / `LocalAdmin@123` (`LocalDevDataSeeder`).

request.description: Saves `ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

`UserService.createUserByAdmin`. Allowed roles: ADMIN, IT_ADMIN, SUPPORT (USER/SERVICE_PROVIDER → 403).
Password: 8–100 chars (no complexity rule on this endpoint). Email is marked verified. Returns **201**.
Admin create rejects customer roles; customers sign up themselves.
Paged, newest first. Only USER and SERVICE_PROVIDER accounts are ever listed (staff accounts are not).

`role` = USER | SERVICE_PROVIDER, `status` = active | disabled, `search` matches name/email/phone,
`page` (0-based), `size` (1–100, default 20).
Any role, including staff.
`isActive:false` deactivates the account and revokes all its refresh tokens.

The JWT is still validly signed, but `JwtAuthenticationFilter` checks `users.is_active` on every request →
**401** `{"code":"ACCOUNT_DELETED","message":"Account has been deactivated."}`.

item.name: 10 · RBAC in action (SUPPORT, USER, anonymous)
item.description:
Shows how the service answers when a caller lacks the required role or token.

**Important:** for a denied or unauthenticated request the service responds **302 Found → `/oauth2/authorize/google`**
(Spring's OAuth2 login entry point), not 401/403. These requests have *Automatically follow redirects* turned off so you
can see the 302. See `docs/onboarding/04-security-jwt-rbac.md`.

request.description: Saves `SUPPORT_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
Any authenticated role can use the self-service endpoints.
`/api/admin/**` requires ROLE_ADMIN or ROLE_IT_ADMIN.

item.name: 11 · Delete accounts
item.description: Run last: these remove the test accounts created above.

request.description: JWT required. Needs a **verified** phone on the account (done in folders 03/06). OTP sent by SMS (console).

Soft delete (`UserService.performSoftDelete`): refresh tokens revoked, email/phone replaced by placeholders,
`isActive=false`. The body on a DELETE is intentional.

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.
401 `ACCOUNT_DELETED` from `JwtAuthenticationFilter`.

`UserController.deleteAccountById`. Allowed when the caller **is** that user, or the caller's DB role is `ADMIN`
(IT_ADMIN is not included here). Soft delete.
Irreversible: deletes the user row and its refresh tokens, sessions, trusted devices, delete OTPs and lockouts.

item.name: 12 · Social sign-in (needs real provider credentials)
item.description:
Google and Apple sign-in verify tokens issued by Google/Apple, so they only succeed with real client ids configured
(`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID`, `APPLE_BUNDLE_ID`). Locally they answer 401
"not configured" / "invalid token" — that is expected. The Apple **email OTP** pair works locally.

request.description:
Public. `GoogleAuthService`. `idToken` from the Google SDK on the phone. `role` USER | SERVICE_PROVIDER,
`mode` login | signup (empty = log in or auto-register). Structured 401 codes: `ROLE_CONFLICT`, `NOT_REGISTERED`,
`ALREADY_REGISTERED`.

Public. Used when Apple did not share an email: the app collects one and proves ownership with a 6-digit code
(10-minute expiry). Console prints it under `EMAIL TYPE: Login OTP`.

Public. Returns `{verified:true, verificationToken}` (HS512, 10 minutes).

**Before sending:** copy the 6-digit code from the service console (`OTP CODE: ...`) into the `OTP` environment variable.

Public. `AppleAuthService`. Either `identityToken` (from Apple) or `verificationToken` (from the step above).
Returns 401 "Apple Sign-In is not configured" unless `APPLE_BUNDLE_ID` is set.

Spring Security `oauth2Login`. Redirects (302) to Google's consent page; the callback is `/oauth2/callback/google`
and responds with `LoginResponse` JSON. Not used by the mobile app. Open in a browser with real credentials.

item.name: 13 · Logout
item.description: Logout revokes **one refresh token**. Access tokens are not revoked; they expire after 24 h.

request.description: Public. Always 200, even for an unknown token.
Logout-revoked tokens get no grace window.
